category.title: Space Science Olympiad
category.description: Preparation for EHF National Space Science Olympiad

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?

explanation.text: The Sun is actually a star! It is the closest star to Earth and the center of our solar system.
explanation.trivia: The Sun is so huge that you could fit about 1.3 million Earths inside it!

questions.question: Which of these planets is the smallest in our Solar System and closest to the Sun?

explanation.text: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and the closest to the Sun.
explanation.trivia: Even though it's the closest to the Sun, Mercury is NOT the hottest planet. Venus is hotter because of its thick atmosphere!

questions.question: In August 2023, India made history by landing Chandrayaan-3 near which part of the Moon?

explanation.text: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander successfully touched down near the lunar south pole.
explanation.trivia: India became the first country ever to land a spacecraft near the Moon's rugged south pole!

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?

options.content: The Earth spinning on its axis
The Sun moving around the Earth

explanation.text: As the Earth rotates on its axis, one side faces the Sun (Day) while the other side faces away (Night).
explanation.trivia: The Earth spins incredibly fast! If you are standing on the equator, you are moving at about 1,000 miles per hour!

questions.question: What is the name of ISRO's upcoming mission that aims to send Indian astronauts into space?

explanation.text: The Gaganyaan mission is designed to demonstrate human spaceflight capability by launching a crew into an orbit of 400 km.
explanation.trivia: 'Gaganyaan' means 'Celestial Vehicle' in Sanskrit. The Indian astronauts training for this mission are called 'Gaganauts'!

questions.question: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet' because of rusty iron dust on its surface?

explanation.text: Mars appears red because its surface is covered in iron oxide, which is the exact same material that makes rust on Earth!
explanation.trivia: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the entire solar system. It is nearly three times taller than Mount Everest!

questions.question: Who was the first Indian citizen to travel into space?

explanation.text: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma flew aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11 rocket in 1984, becoming the first Indian in space.
explanation.trivia: When the Indian Prime Minister asked him how India looked from space, he famously replied 'Sare Jahan Se Achha' (Better than the entire world)!

questions.question: Why does the Moon shine brightly in the night sky?

options.content: It reflects light from the Sun
It reflects light from the Earth
It is covered in glowing rocks

explanation.text: The Moon doesn't emit its own light. It acts like a giant mirror in space, reflecting the Sun's light down to Earth.
explanation.trivia: The footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the Moon will probably stay there for millions of years because there is no wind to blow them away!

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our Solar System, famous for its Great Red Spot?

explanation.text: Jupiter is a gas giant and by far the largest planet in our solar system.
explanation.trivia: The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is actually a giant, swirling storm that is larger than Earth and has been raging for hundreds of years!

questions.question: Where is the main Asteroid Belt located in our Solar System?

explanation.text: The main asteroid belt is a ring of rocky debris orbiting the Sun between the inner and outer planets.
explanation.trivia: Even though there are millions of asteroids in the belt, if you gathered them all together, they would still be smaller than our Moon!

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a mass more than two and a half times that of all the other planets in the solar system combined.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars is often called the Red Planet because iron oxide on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.

questions.question: What is the name of our galaxy?
questions.explanation: Our solar system is located in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.question: Which planet has the most prominent ring system?
questions.explanation: Saturn is famous for its extensive and bright ring system.

questions.question: What is the hottest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Venus is the hottest planet due to its thick atmosphere which creates a strong greenhouse effect.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system has the most known moons?

explanation.text: Saturn currently holds the record for the most known moons in the solar system, officially surpassing Jupiter recently.
explanation.trivia: Saturn has over 140 known moons! The largest one is Titan, which is actually bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.question: What is the famous comet that can be seen from Earth every 75-76 years?

explanation.text: Halley's Comet is a 'short-period' comet visible from Earth every 75–76 years.
explanation.trivia: The famous author Mark Twain was born shortly after Halley's Comet appeared in 1835, and he predicted he would 'go out with it' in 1910—and he was right!

questions.question: Which of these is the largest dwarf planet in our solar system?

explanation.text: Pluto is the largest known dwarf planet by volume, although Eris is slightly more massive.
explanation.trivia: In 2006, Pluto was reclassified from a 'planet' to a 'dwarf planet' because it hasn't cleared its neighboring region of other objects.

questions.question: What is a 'shooting star' actually called in astronomy when it enters Earth's atmosphere?

explanation.text: When space rocks burn up in Earth's atmosphere causing a bright streak of light, they are called Meteors.
explanation.trivia: If a meteor survives its fiery journey and hits the ground, it is then called a 'Meteorite'!

questions.question: Which moon is the only place beyond Earth where humans have set foot?

explanation.text: Earth's Moon (also called Luna) is the only celestial body visited by humans, starting with the Apollo 11 mission in 1969.
explanation.trivia: A total of 12 people have walked on the Moon, all of them American astronauts during the Apollo program.

questions.question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched into space?

explanation.text: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union in 1957, marking the beginning of the Space Age.
explanation.trivia: It was about the size of a beach ball and its only job was to transmit a simple 'beep-beep' radio signal back to Earth!

questions.question: What was the primary goal of India's historic Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)?

options.content: To land a rover on Mars
To orbit Mars and study its surface and atmosphere
To bring Martian soil back to Earth

explanation.text: Mangalyaan was an orbital mission designed to study Martian topography, morphology, and the atmosphere.
explanation.trivia: ISRO achieved this on its very first attempt, and it was the most cost-effective Mars mission ever done—costing less than the Hollywood movie 'Gravity'!

questions.question: Which space telescope was launched in 1990 and has taken some of the most famous deep-space photos?

explanation.text: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth above the atmosphere, allowing it to capture incredibly clear images of the universe.
explanation.trivia: When Hubble was first launched, its primary mirror had a tiny flaw (1/50th the thickness of a human hair) which made images blurry until astronauts fixed it in space!

questions.question: Who was the first woman to travel into space?

explanation.text: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963 aboard the Vostok 6.
explanation.trivia: During her mission, she orbited the Earth 48 times and spent almost 3 days in space!

questions.question: Which female astronaut holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman?

explanation.text: NASA astronaut Christina Koch spent 328 consecutive days on the International Space Station.
explanation.trivia: She also participated in the first all-female spacewalk with her colleague Jessica Meir!

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Solar System?

explanation.text: We live in the Milky Way, a barred spiral galaxy containing an estimated 100-400 billion stars.
explanation.trivia: If you look up at a very dark night sky, the Milky Way looks like a hazy, glowing band of milk stretched across the stars.

questions.question: What is a black hole?

options.content: A star that produces dark light
A region of space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape

explanation.text: A black hole is incredibly dense with gravity so intense that it sucks in everything around it, including light.
explanation.trivia: The boundary around a black hole where nothing can escape is terrifyingly called the 'Event Horizon'.

questions.question: What is the closest major galaxy to the Milky Way?

explanation.text: The Andromeda Galaxy is our closest large galactic neighbor, located about 2.5 million light-years away.
explanation.trivia: The Milky Way and Andromeda are currently rushing toward each other and will eventually crash and merge into one giant galaxy billions of years from now!

questions.question: What unit of measurement is used to measure the immense distances between stars?

explanation.text: A light-year is the distance that light travels in one Earth year, which is nearly 6 trillion miles!
explanation.trivia: Because light takes time to travel, when you look at a star that is 10 light-years away, you are actually seeing how it looked 10 years ago in the past!

questions.question: What are exoplanets?

options.content: Planets that orbit stars outside our solar system

explanation.text: An exoplanet (extrasolar planet) is any planet that orbits a star other than our own Sun.
explanation.trivia: Scientists have discovered thousands of exoplanets! Some are strange worlds where it rains glass sideways, or planets made mostly of diamond!

questions.question: Which fundamental force is responsible for keeping the planets in orbit around the Sun?

explanation.text: Gravity is the invisible force of attraction between all masses in the universe, keeping planets tethered to their stars.
explanation.trivia: Without gravity, if you jumped up, you would float off into space and never come down!

questions.question: According to Albert Einstein, gravity is actually the curving of what?

explanation.text: In his General Theory of Relativity, Einstein showed that massive objects like the Sun warp the fabric of space and time around them.
explanation.trivia: Imagine putting a heavy bowling ball on a trampoline. It creates a dip. If you roll a marble on the trampoline, it orbits the dip. That's exactly how gravity works in spacetime!

questions.question: What happens to time as you get closer to a massive object with intense gravity, like a black hole?

explanation.text: This effect is called 'gravitational time dilation'. Gravity literally stretches time, making it move slower relative to an observer further away.
explanation.trivia: Because of this, your head is actually aging very, very slightly faster than your feet because your feet are closer to Earth's gravity!

questions.question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?

explanation.text: Light travels at a blistering speed of 299,792 kilometers per second (or about 186,000 miles per second) in a vacuum.
explanation.trivia: It is the ultimate speed limit of the universe! Nothing with mass can ever travel faster than the speed of light.

questions.question: What mysterious invisible substance makes up about 85% of the matter in the universe, holding galaxies together?

explanation.text: Dark Matter does not emit, absorb, or reflect light, but scientists know it exists because of its gravitational pull on visible galaxies.
explanation.trivia: Even though it makes up most of the universe, scientists still don't know exactly what Dark Matter is made of!
